items.transcription_or_faithful_content: For t=1,...,T: adversary chooses y_t in [0,1] and keeps it secret; player chooses x_t in [0,1]; y_t is revealed and the loss is (x_t-y_t)^2.
items.notes: Initial move order is secret outcome, then prediction, then full outcome revelation. No factor 1/2 in the loss.

items.reason: Motivates the choice of winning condition without adding mathematical assumptions.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Temporarily assume iid draws from a fixed distribution on [0,1], chosen at the beginning. Predicting its mean has expected total loss sigma^2 T and cannot be improved.
items.notes: Illustrative stochastic benchmark only; not an assumption of the later adversarial theorem. Its mean-optimality calculation is not supplied.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: The quantities are nonnegative; sublinear growth of (1.1) is equivalent to (1.2) tending to zero as T tends to infinity.
items.notes: Nonnegativity is said of this stochastic benchmark, not asserted here for every realized hindsight regret.
The minimum is outside the expectation in this display. It must not be silently replaced by expected realized hindsight minimum.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Remove the assumption on how data are generated and consider any arbitrary sequence y_t. If the algorithm is deterministic, remove the expectation because there is no stochasticity anymore.
items.notes: The text explicitly qualifies removing expectation by determinism. It does not give a full randomized-strategy lower-bound convention.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Regret_T := sum_{t=1}^T (x_t-y_t)^2 - min_{x in [0,1]} sum_{t=1}^T (x-y_t)^2; success is sublinear growth in T. The comparator is one fixed best choice in hindsight.
items.notes: Unnormalized cumulative regret. Full realized-sequence minimum, not minimum expected loss.

items.reason: Forward-looking motivation about convex optimization and machine learning; no proof dependency.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: The single competitor is retained for most of the book; a sequence of competitors is considered in Chapter 14.
items.notes: A dynamic-comparator target is not this guessing problem.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: For V subset R^d, predictions x_t in V, losses ell_t:V->R and arbitrary fixed u in V, Regret_T(u):=sum_t ell_t(x_t)-sum_t ell_t(u).
The algorithm does not know u or the corresponding regret to guarantee its bound. No-regret means for every fixed u in V, lim_{T->infinity} Regret_T(u)/T <= 0.
items.notes: Transcribes the source use of lim without repairing it to limsup.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Regret also depends on ell_1,...,ell_T; this dependence is suppressed.

items.reason: The general possibility of predictions in W strictly containing V is not invoked for the [0,1] guessing problem.
Applications to clicks, routing, games and stochastic optimization are motivation, not guessing-problem proof inputs.

anchor.region: paragraph Let us now go back

items.reason: Pedagogical transition, without new mathematical content.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: The game can be won also if the adversary picks its number after observing our choice; no assumption is made about how numbers are decided.
items.notes: Strengthens the upper-bound adversary model beyond the opening secret-number protocol. It is not a formal specification of randomized lower-bound quantifiers.

items.reason: Explains why statistical prediction intuition is inadequate under adversarial changes; no new lemma or proof step.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: x_T^star := argmin_{x in [0,1]} sum_{t=1}^T (x-y_t)^2 = (1/T) sum_{t=1}^T y_t.
items.notes: The source calls this immediate and gives no derivation; for positive T the displayed average is the intended scalar minimizer, despite argmin being written as a scalar.

anchor.region: paragraph Now, given that we do not know the future

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: We cannot use x_T^star as each prediction because we do not know the future; the past is known, and the proposed strategy tracks the past minimizer.
For t>=2, x_t=x_{t-1}^star=(1/(t-1)) sum_{i=1}^{t-1} y_i; in the first round guess any number between 0 and 1. This is Follow-the-Leader (FTL).
items.notes: The subsequent Theorem 1.3 fixes the initial choice to 0.5, unlike this broader description.

items.reason: Announces first-principles proof and a lemma; no additional obligation beyond Lemma 1.2.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Let V subset R^d and ell_t:V->R be arbitrary. Assume x_t^star in argmin_{x in V} sum_{i=1}^t ell_i(x) exists. Then sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_t^star) <= sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_T^star).
items.notes: Existence at every required prefix is an explicit premise. No convexity or probability premise.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Induct on T. At T=1, ell_1(x_1^star) <= ell_1(x_1^star).
For T>=2, cancel equal final terms to reduce the target to sum_{t=1}^{T-1} ell_t(x_t^star) <= sum_{t=1}^{T-1} ell_t(x_T^star).
The induction hypothesis gives sum_{t=1}^{T-1} ell_t(x_t^star) <= sum_{t=1}^{T-1} ell_t(x_{T-1}^star).
sum_{t=1}^{T-1} ell_t(x_{T-1}^star) <= sum_{t=1}^{T-1} ell_t(x_T^star), because x_{T-1}^star minimizes prefix cumulative loss and x_T^star is in V.
Chain the induction hypothesis and prefix-minimality inequalities to prove (1.3), hence the lemma.

items.reason: Informal interpretation of the lemma; does not add a dependency.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: With this lemma, we can now prove that the regret will grow sublinearly; in particular, it will be at most logarithmic in time. Note that we will not prove that our strategy is minimax optimal, even if it is possible to show that the logarithmic dependence on time is unavoidable for this problem.
items.notes: Exact prose transcription, normalizing line breaks only. No displayed lower bound, constants, horizon threshold, probability qualifier, or citation accompanies this claim.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Let y_1,...,y_T in [0,1] be arbitrary. Let x_t=x_{t-1}^star:=(1/(t-1)) sum_{i=1}^{t-1} y_i for t>=2 and x_1=x_0^star:=0.5. Then Regret_T=sum_{t=1}^T (x_t-y_t)^2-min_{x in [0,1]} sum_{t=1}^T (x-y_t)^2 <= 4+4 ln T.
items.notes: Positive integer horizon is implicit in rounds, averaging and ln T. This is an upper bound for deterministic FTL, not a lower bound for all algorithms.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Upper bounding the sum with an integral. Plot compares 1/x and 1/(x-1) with gray rectangles.
items.notes: Supports the upper harmonic-sum estimate, not a logarithmic lower bound.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Regret_T = sum_t (x_{t-1}^star-y_t)^2 - sum_t (x_T^star-y_t)^2 <= sum_t [(x_{t-1}^star-y_t)^2-(x_t^star-y_t)^2].
items.notes: Uses the FTL rule, mean characterization, and Lemma 1.2 with squared losses.
Uses x_0^star=0.5, x_1^star=y_1, and y_1 in [0,1].

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: (x_{t-1}^star-y_t)^2-(x_t^star-y_t)^2 = (x_{t-1}^star+x_t^star-2y_t)(x_{t-1}^star-x_t^star) <= |x_{t-1}^star+x_t^star-2y_t| |x_{t-1}^star-x_t^star| <= 2|x_{t-1}^star-x_t^star|.

items.notes: This is an upper bound using bounded y_i and the triangle inequality, not a lower bound.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: sum_{t=1}^T 1/t <= 1 + integral_{2}^{T+1} 1/(t-1) dt = 1 + ln T.
items.notes: The explanatory paragraph starts at the bottom of printed p5; Figure 1.1 supports the inequality.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Combining the regret harmonic-sum bound and the integral estimate gives Theorem 1.3.

items.transcription_or_faithful_content: Lemma 1.2 replaces the single best guess by prefix leaders; predicting x_{t-1}^star while |x_t^star-x_{t-1}^star| decays like 1/t gives sublinear total regret.
items.notes: A paraphrase of the upper proof, not an independent alternative route.
